In thirty years, two of my findings were overturned. I remember them better than anything I got right. In both cases the fact was correct, but my sentence was too strong. When you write that a person was negligent, you are not describing an event any more. You are making a legal claim, and somebody will test it. So I write it would appear that. Some people say that is weak. It is not weak. It is honest about how much I know. If the evidence gets stronger later, I can make the sentence stronger. And there is a second reason. A careful finding is easier for the company to accept.
